title: Sequence-to-Sequence Modeling
description: Prepare to explain the sequence-to-sequence paradigm in the Transformer era.
content:
**Sequence-to-sequence modeling** - input sequence in, different-length output sequence out - is the natural fit for translation, summarization and dialogue. In the Transformer era this role belongs to **encoder-decoder** models: an encoder reads the source with bidirectional self-attention, a decoder generates the target with causal self-attention, and **cross-attention** lets every decoding step attend to all encoder states - the Transformer incarnation of the attention mechanism that replaced the seq2seq bottleneck.

**T5 (Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer)** unifies everything into text-to-text: every task - translation, classification, QA, summarization - is cast as generating an output string from an input string, with a **task prefix** like 'translate English to German: ...' or 'summarize: ...' telling the model what to do. One architecture, one pretraining objective (span corruption: mask spans of tokens and predict them), one decoding procedure for all tasks.

**BART** is a sibling encoder-decoder pretrained by **denoising**: the input text is corrupted (spans masked, tokens deleted, sentences permuted) and the model must reconstruct the clean original.

> Choosing the architecture:
> • Understanding only -> encoder-only (BERT)
> • Open-ended generation -> decoder-only (GPT)
> • Conditional generation with a well-defined output -> encoder-decoder (T5, BART)
